say.t: A bright meeting room, plenty of space. Everyone is waiting.
Your boss, and your partner: Lao Wang. He stands in front of the projector holding a pen. Its cap went missing long ago.
Future Intelligence. Series B. Signed.

Only then does the room dare to make a sound. Someone slaps the table, someone twists open a bottle of water, someone holds a phone up at the projector. You sit closest to the projector: you can't see the whole screen, but the words are clear.
{bossCalls}. Vivi, you, the few of us who founded this: we rowed a small boat upstream all the way. Now the boat is finally big.
Yes. My share isn't much, but when the base is this big, I'll ride up with it. That's good. That's really good.
Someone stops you in the corridor. This is Chen Weiwei, Vivi, your partner.
In her hands, a stack of printed papers, highlighter all over them: the marks of someone reading and getting excited at once.
She's always like this. She prints documents out and reads them word by word. She prints so much that the printer in her office only gets black ink.
You know that until you have read all of it, you aren't going anywhere.
Hear me out. If this becomes a product, it has to be you. Only you can build it.
By the time she finishes, it is noon at the end of the corridor and the light is behind her. You can't see her face, only the highlighter lines, lit one by one.
The hundredth employee arrives in the afternoon. His backpack still on, he wipes his hand on his trousers before holding it out.
Hello, teacher… I mean, hello, boss…
You tell him {calledBy} is fine. He says it over to himself once, like saving a file.
The red envelope comes in the evening. The family table, two more dishes than usual.
{nick}, eat.
Halfway through dinner a red envelope is pushed against your bowl, so thick its flap won't close. You say you have money, really, you have money now.
We know, we know you have money. Our child's done well, we're celebrating. This is celebrating, not giving you money.
You put the envelope in your pocket. The pocket bulges, and you don't sit up straight for the rest of the meal.
Then the models got better every year. Something you had spent two years building, one day someone else built with one sentence.
The client said, we'll just have AI do it ourselves. Nobody did anything wrong. The price of doing this thing fell to zero.
The year before last I still thought writing SQL was a skill.
With every pivot a few more desks went empty. A hundred, seventy, fifty.
The last time in the office was an evening. The AI-native reform: the office was given up, everyone works from home.
No need to come in. I fought for that for you.
Lao Wang took the lion's share. He has been financially free for a while now.
Vivi married a local. Her home is near where the office used to be.
Your small share wasn't worth much by the time you could sell it. Going back to your hometown: you thought about it, and set it aside again.
The lease on this rented room was renewed for a year. Then for another.
Dreaming all that, it doesn't feel like another life.
…It was all just the last year or two.
